extracted.intended_audience: USPTO employees (patent examiners and supervisors), former USPTO employees, and patent practitioners interacting with the Office
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of MPEP Chapter 1700 policies and procedural standards governing USPTO personnel conduct (testimony, opinions, post-employment practice), Official Gazette content, PALM docket/time reporting, dissemination of court/PTAB decisions, and information sources/online systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office personnel not to express opinion on validity/patentability/enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Every USPTO employee must refuse to express to any person any opinion as to the validity or invalidity of, or the patentability or unpatentability of any claim in any U.S. patent, except to the extent necessary to carry out specified Office proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (A) examination of a reissue application of the patent; (B) supplemental examination or reexamination proceeding; (C) interference or derivation proceeding involving the patent; (D) inter partes or post-grant review. Public policy presumes patents valid (35 U.S.C. 282). Employees must not pursue private bounties for prior art or accept outside payments for prior art searches (may subject to disciplinary action). When asked for a field of search, examiners should inquire whether the invention has been patented; if patented, no field of search should be suggested. Employees who examined an application should not discuss whether a reference was considered or whether a claim would have been allowed — the file must speak for itself. Practitioners' inquiries on these matters must be refused; such refusal is not discourteous or an expression of opinion. Definitions/exceptions in 37 CFR 104.1 and 104.21 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office personnel will not testify except under 37 CFR Part 104 Subpart C
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO policy forbids employees (including patent examiners) from appearing as witnesses or giving testimony in legal proceedings except as specified by 37 CFR Part 104, Subpart C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees who are asked to testify or receive a subpoena must immediately notify the Office of the USPTO General Counsel. Requests for testimony must comply with 37 CFR Part 104 Subpart C; employees testifying contrary to policy may be dismissed. A request for testimony should be made to General Counsel at least 10 working days prior to expected testimony (15 days required for depositions between Nov 15 and Jan 15). Depositions in pending ex parte reexamination proceedings will generally be denied. Any authorized testimony is limited to facts within the employee's personal knowledge; expert/opinion, hypothetical or speculative questions are prohibited. Several court decisions limit permissible testimony regarding quasi‑judicial functions and mental processes (cases cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on permissible questions to USPTO quasi‑judicial employees
rubrics_metrics.description: When USPTO employees are authorized to testify, questions directed to certain topics are impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impermissible topics include: (1) detailed background, expertise, qualifications to examine, usual practice or whether a procedure in an Office manual was followed, consultations with other Office employees, understanding of inventions, prior art, documents, manuals, regulations or laws, responsibilities of others, or reliance on particular facts; (2) the manner and extent to which the employee considered or studied material in performing a quasi‑judicial function; (3) bases, reasons, mental processes, analyses, or conclusions of the employee in performing quasi‑judicial functions. Requests for testimony must comply with 37 CFR 104.22(c) and be in writing. Conditions (A)-(E) (case style, civil action number, district, judge, counsel contacts; agreement not to ask questions precluded by 37 CFR 104.23; compliance with Federal Rules and notice; convenient deposition place; supply transcript to USPTO) must be met to obviate a subpoena; otherwise subpoena required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on employees testifying as experts or giving opinion testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners and other USPTO employees performing or assisting in quasi‑judicial functions are forbidden to testify as experts or to express opinions as to the validity of any patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorized to testify, employees are limited to facts within personal knowledge and are prohibited from answering hypothetical or speculative questions or giving expert opinions. Court precedent (e.g., Fischer & Porter; In re Mayewsky; Shaffer Tool Works) supports restriction of testimony to factual matters and avoidance of mental processes or expertise probing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on officers and employees as to interest in patents (35 U.S.C. 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 4, USPTO officers and employees shall be incapable, during appointment and for one year thereafter, of applying for a patent or acquiring any patent or right or interest in any patent except by inheritance/bequest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents applied for thereafter they shall not be entitled to any priority date earlier than one year after termination. An Office employee named as inventor will be presumed incapable of signing the inventor's oath/declaration under 35 U.S.C. 4; for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, a substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 may be filed in lieu of the oath/declaration without contacting the employee. See MPEP § 309.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on practice in patent matters (37 CFR 11.10) — who may practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Only registrants under § 11.6 or individuals given limited recognition under § 11.9(a) or (b) may prosecute patent applications of others before the USPTO or represent others in proceedings before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government employees and others must follow these registration rules to practice before the Office; separate post‑employment restrictions apply as described in § 11.10(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑employment restrictions and written undertaking (37 CFR 11.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Former USPTO employees who served in the examining corps or elsewhere may not practice before the Office after termination unless they sign a written undertaking limiting representation in matters they participated in personally and substantially or that were under their official responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undertaking (b)(1): not to knowingly act as agent/attorney for or assist others before the Office in connection with any particular patent/application in which the employee participated personally and substantially as an employee. Undertaking (b)(2): not to act within two years after termination as agent/attorney or assist in representation before the Office in connection with any particular patent/application that was pending under the employee’s official responsibility within one year prior to termination. Definitions in (b)(3) clarify terms 'represent', 'assist', 'particular patent or patent application', and 'participate personally and substantially.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'participate personally and substantially'
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation is personal and substantial when exercised through decision, approval, disapproval, recommendation, rendering of advice, investigation or otherwise; includes direct participation and participation by a subordinate directed by the former employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial means involvement of significance to the matter or that forms a basis for reasonable appearance of significance — more than official responsibility, knowledge, perfunctory involvement, or administrative/peripheral involvement. A finding of substantiality should consider both effort devoted and importance of the effort. A single critical act (e.g., approving) may be substantial. Participation must be related to a particular patent or patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary matters vs. substantial participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation on subjects not directly involving the substantive merits may not be 'substantial' even if time-consuming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An employee reviewing applications solely for administrative control or budgetary purposes typically will not be regarded as having participated substantially, except when those considerations are also the subject of proposed representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of official responsibility in determining substantial participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Official responsibility is distinct from personal and substantial participation but may play a role in determining substantiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official responsibility is defined separately and normally concerns administrative or operating authority; it's not automatically equivalent to substantial participation but can inform the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official responsibility definition and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Official responsibility means the direct administrative or operating authority to approve, disapprove, or otherwise direct government actions, exercised alone or with others and personally or through subordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily determined by statute, regulation, job description or delegation. The Director has official responsibility for all matters; intermediate supervisors have responsibility for matters under employees they supervise. Authority for ancillary administrative matters (budgeting, EEO, PR) usually does not constitute official responsibility for a particular patent/application unless those considerations are the subject of proposed representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to inquire for former employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A former employee has a reasonable duty to inquire whether a patent or application was under their official responsibility; lack of actual knowledge while employed does not excuse restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If facts suggest a relationship of the prior matter to the former office (e.g., technology center, group, art unit), the former employee should make further inquiry. It is prudent to maintain records of application numbers actually acted upon and those under official responsibility the employee has not acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self‑disqualification does not avoid lifetime restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Self‑disqualification cannot be used by a former employee to avoid post‑employment restrictions where they otherwise had official responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an employee who self‑disqualifies and does not participate personally and substantially in a particular matter is not subject to the lifetime restriction of paragraph (b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of the two‑year restriction period
rubrics_metrics.description: The two‑year restriction in § 11.10(b)(2) is measured from the date the employee's official responsibility in a particular area ends, not from the termination of service unless those dates coincide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition applies to all particular patents/applications subject to such official responsibility in the one‑year period before termination of that responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section does not supplant other post‑employment statutory restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The section imposes restrictions generally parallel to 18 U.S.C. 207(a) and (b)(1) but does not interpret those statutes or other post‑employment restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former employees should not assume conduct not prohibited by this section is permissible under other laws and are encouraged to contact the Department of Commerce for information on applicable restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on employees prosecuting or aiding prosecution before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office employee may not prosecute or aid in any manner in the prosecution of any patent application before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general prohibition reinforcing separation of Office personnel and private practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice before the Office by government employees subject to conflict laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice before the Office by government employees is subject to applicable conflict of interest laws, regulations, or professional responsibility codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must observe any additional limitations beyond MPEP/37 CFR requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette — content for patents (required information)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette — Patents reports issued patents and related items and for each patent may give a prescribed set of bibliographic and content information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As to each patent, information may include: (A) Patent number; (B) Title of the invention; (C) Name of inventor(s), city, and state/country; (D) Assignee name, city, state/country if assigned; (E) Applicant's name, city, state/country; (F) Filing date and application number; (G) For reissue patents: original patent number/issue date and original application number/filing date; (H) U.S. benefit application data; (I) PCT/international design application data; (J) Foreign priority application data; (K) Patent Application Publication Number and Publication date; (L) International classification; (M) CPC classification; (N) U.S. classification by class/subclass; (O) Number of claims; (P) Selected figure of the drawing; (Q) A claim or claims. eOG:P allows browsing by classification, patentee, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette — Trademarks content and features
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette — Trademarks is published electronically and contains trademark illustrations and registration-related lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes illustration of each trademark published for opposition, alphabetical and classified lists of registered trademarks, index of registrants, list of canceled registrations, and list of renewed registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM is the official automated system for application records and examiner time/activity/dockets
rubrics_metrics.description: PALM (Patent Application Locating and Monitoring) is the USPTO automated data management system for retrieval and online updating of the computer record of each patent application and for maintaining examiner time, activity, and docket records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information retrieval via PALM intranet; transactions entered by keyed entries or dropdown menus. Data include classification, examiner docket, attorney, inventor, status, prosecution history, and paper application location. PALM simultaneously records changes, incoming/outgoing communications, transfers to/from dockets, and other updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket reports generated by PALM and their purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: PALM generates various docket reports to reflect examiner workloads and application statuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports include: individual examiner new and amended docket (lists regular, special, expedited applications in priority order); individual examiner rejected application docket; individual examiner new application profile (totals of new apps per month); and various summaries at art unit, Technology Center, and corps levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biweekly Time and Activity reporting and examiner responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: All examiner time and activity reporting is on a biweekly basis; Web Time and Attendance entries feed PALM productivity computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biweekly Examiner Time and Activity Report lists, by application number, all applications for which actions have been counted during the period, indicating type of action and examiner time data, action summary, and cumulative summaries. Examiner should check their report to verify all applications worked on are properly listed. Certain actions (examiner's amendments, reexamination actions, interview summaries, transfers, supplemental Office actions and miscellaneous letters without reply period) are reported by legal instrument examiners but may not be listed on the Biweekly report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting of First Action on the Merits (FAOM)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAOM is credited the first time an examiner performs an Office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions on the merits consist of rejections (final and non‑final), Ex parte Quayle actions, and allowances. If first action is restriction/election and second action is on the merits, the second may be a FAOM; PALM will automatically determine FAOM status and credit Second/Subsequent FAOM appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting of disposals and what constitutes disposal credit
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner receives 'disposal' credit for specified actions; disposals are used in performance evaluation of art units/TCs and at the Office level differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disposal credits include: (A) Allowance; (B) Abandonment; (C) Requests for Continued Examination; (D) Examiner's Answer; (E) International Preliminary Examination Report; (F) Statutory Invention Registration (SIR) disposal (only after a FAOM); (G) Institution of an Interference or Derivation proceeding where application would be in condition for allowance but for the interference/derivation. At Office level, disposals consist only of allowances and abandonments. No disposal credit for allowance/abandonment after an Examiner's Answer or court/PTAB decision, though actions are indicated on reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction procedures for PALM reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If information is missing or incorrect on Biweekly Examiner Time and Activity Reports, examiners must notify supervisors and PALM support to have corrections made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify SPE and legal instrument examiner or PALM troubleshooter with pertinent info (examining hours, application number, type of action). Changes are entered into PALM and reflected on the next Biweekly report. If missing/incorrect on last biweekly report of a quarter (except fiscal year end) notify immediately for adjustment; changes will not be reflected in the previous quarter’s reports unless SPE manually adjusts. Special correction cycle at fiscal year end ensures PALM reports are correct for rating period; report corrections for last biweekly of fiscal year must be made promptly to be reflected in final annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of court and PTAB decisions within USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures exist to forward and circulate precedential court and Patent Trial and Appeal Board opinions to relevant USPTO officials and examiners to reinforce examination quality and update practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of the Solicitor forwards precedential court opinions to the Commissioner for Patents, who forwards them to TC Directors, Office of Patent Training, and Director of Patent Quality Assurance. TC Directors make copies available to supervisors and other individuals; encouraged to discuss in staff meetings. PTAB decisions are returned to the examiner who must act consistent with the decision unless rehearing is requested; TC Directors/supervisors may circulate PTAB decisions depending on subject matter. If a decision significantly adds to the law or affects USPTO policy/practice, it may prompt an internal memorandum, incorporation into MPEP, and updates to training materials. Chain-of-command and consultation with Deputy Commissioner/Commissioner and Office counsel are required to formulate guidance; communications may be via Official Gazette or internal memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO information sources and contact points
rubrics_metrics.description: General information and assistance about patents/trademarks and USPTO services are available via designated contact centers, online resources, and public facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO Contact Center phone numbers and hours provided; Inventors Assistance Center hours; Public Search Facility and library locations/hours listed. EBC assists customers with EFS‑Web and PAIR, offers online instructional material and one‑on‑one support (hours and contact info provided). PCT Help Desk contact info provided for PCT questions. Office of Public Records provides copies ordering. Assignment Services, Petitions Help Desk, Receipts Accounting Division, PatentIn support, and other specific contacts are enumerated. USPTO cannot recommend particular attorneys/agents but provides a register of practitioners online.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO online systems and databases — descriptions and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of key USPTO electronic systems (Patent Grants Database, Patent Applications Database, PAIR, IFW, AOTW, GPSN, EFS‑Web) and their appropriate uses and limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Grants Database: full‑text patents since 1976 and full‑page images since 1790. Patent Applications Database: published applications since March 15, 2001. PAIR: public PAIR provides issued patents, published apps, and domestic priority claims; private PAIR provides unpublished app info to applicants/registered practitioners with Customer Number. IFW is the official electronic image file for scanned applications; for IFW files, IFW is the official file and original paper sheets are not accessible. Non‑patent literature may be viewed using private PAIR or obtained from Office of Public Records. GPSN provides machine translations (subset of Chinese patents) but translations are not authoritative and may omit/transliterate words ("***"); original images are authoritative. EFS‑Web allows electronic filing of applications — see EFS‑Web legal framework. AOTW provides assignment info recorded since Aug 1980. Offices provide links, forms, fee lists, and filing options online.
